question.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=1$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(1)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(1)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨1,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(1) & =⟨0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(1)$ and ${r}^{″}(1)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1) & =⟨1,1,0⟩\times ⟨0,-1,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & \,\,-1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(1) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(1){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(1)\times {r}^{″}(1)‖}=\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{3}}{\,1\,}=2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
